subject: Unexpected rate-limiter guardrail triggered — proposed short-term contract exception and evidence delivery
messages:
From: Tanya Rao <tanya@nebulacorp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@nebulacorp.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: 429s across our production tenant since 08:20PT — impacting chat flows

Hi Olga,

We started seeing a spike in 429 responses across our production routes at ~08:20 PT this morning. Errors are intermittent but are affecting our conversational UI — backlog and user-facing timeouts. Graphs attached (usage-graph.png) and a short log dump from one of the failed requests.

We didn't change our integration or traffic profile — same traffic as yesterday — so this is unexpected. Can you confirm if anything changed on Redwood side (rate-limiter config, guardrails, policy rollouts) that could cause an immediate 429 for our tenant? We're preparing an incident call if needed.

Thanks,
Tanya Rao
Sr. Engineering Manager, NebulaCorp

Attachments: usage-graph.png, excerpt.log

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tanya Rao <tanya@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 429s across our production tenant since 08:20PT — quick triage and next steps

Hi Tanya — thanks for the heads up and the graphs, sorry for the disruption.

Quick update from triage: I've looped in Ben (AE) and Lauren (CSM) to coordinate. We're standing up an incident room and will gather evidence for you. Could you confirm the customer tenant ID or a single request-id for one of the 429s (if available) so we can map it to our logs?

Immediate plan:
- Ben & I will validate whether any rate-limiter policy changes or rollout jobs touched NebulaCorp's tenant between 07:30–09:00 PT.
- Lauren will prepare a short customer-facing summary and remediation options (throttle exceptions, short-term quota bump, or rollback).
- We'll deliver a config snapshot and usage proof by EOD PST.

I understand this impacts end users — we'll prioritize.

Olga Petrov
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: 429s — initial evidence (config snapshot)

Folks — I grabbed the policy rollout logs and did a quick scan. Initial findings (summary):
- There was a staged rollout of a new "guardrail" policy at 08:05 PT that included an automatic per-tenant emergency cap for anomalous token rates.
- NebulaCorp's tenant matched the anomaly detector rules because their burst pattern briefly exceeded our historic per-minute delta threshold. The rollout script included a target-tier mapping that mistakenly applied the emergency cap to the "standard" tier instead of "trial" tier due to a tag mismatch.
- Result: an immediate per-tenant cap applied and returned 429s for requests that exceeded the emergency cap.

Attached: rl-config-snapshot.txt (policy, rollout id, tenant mapping), and a short annotated timeline.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Revert the rollout entry that applied the emergency cap to NebulaCorp (safe, targeted rollback).
2) Apply a one-time quota exception for NebulaCorp for the next 6 hours while we validate.
3) Offer a one-time service credit to compensate for user impact (Lauren to coordinate the amount with Finance).
4) Postmortem and process fix: make the tag mapping explicit in rollout scripts and add an extra preflight check for tenant-tag disambiguation.

I'll prepare the rollback and the config diff. Olga — want me to push the rollback now and then issue the quota exception?

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rl-config-snapshot.txt

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tanya Rao <tanya@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 429s across our production tenant since 08:20PT — remediation plan and short-term exception

Hi Tanya — thank you for your patience.

Summary of what we found: a guardrail rollout included an emergency per-tenant cap. NebulaCorp incorrectly matched the cap due to a tag mapping bug in the rollout configuration. That cap triggered 429s for requests that exceeded the emergency threshold.

What we're going to do now (immediate):
- Act 1 (now): We will rollback the specific rollout entry that applied the emergency cap to NebulaCorp. This is low-risk and isolated; it will restore pre-rollout behavior within ~3 minutes.
- Act 2 (within 10 minutes): Apply a temporary quota exception to NebulaCorp for 6 hours to cover in-flight traffic while we validate.
- Act 3 (by EOD PST): Deliver config snapshot, annotated timeline, and evidence (rl-config-snapshot.txt + usage graphs).
- Act 4 (by 2027-08-31): Deliver a formal postmortem with corrective actions and timeline for permanent fixes.

Compensation: We're prepared to issue a one-time service credit and a customer goodwill letter. Attached is the proposed credit offer (credit-offer-20270831.pdf). Lauren, please coordinate the exact credit and any contract exception paperwork.

If you approve, we'll proceed with the rollback and apply the temporary quota exception immediately and confirm when traffic returns to normal.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Unexpected rate-limiter guardrail triggered — accepted rollback and next steps

Olga / team —

Thanks for the quick investigation and for the clear remediation plan. Please proceed with the rollback and the 6-hour quota exception. We appreciate the proposed credit — we'll accept it pending the postmortem.

We have a legal/contract note: if you need a short-term amendment to increase our committed capacity for the 6-hour window, please route the paperwork through our procurement team (procurement@nebulacorp.com). Otherwise, a platform-side exception is fine.

Also please include the annotated timeline and the config snapshot in the HubSpot ticket so our SREs can cross-reference.

Thanks — Tanya
